questions.prompt: Two controllers both write joint1/velocity. What does ros2_control allow?
options: Both can be active, but each one only receives half of the gain
Both can be active at once, and the one that writes last wins
Only one can be active; the other cannot claim the command interface
Both can be active if their commands use the same message type
questions.explanation: A command interface has at most one active owner.

questions.prompt: update_rate is 200 Hz. Period in ms.
update_rate 500 Hz and a cycle (read+update+write) of 1.8 ms. Utilization (fraction of the period). Precision 0.01.
PID with kp=3, ki=2, kd=0, dt=0.05, error 1, integral starts at 0 and no saturation. Output u. Precision 0.001.
A mock hardware interface returns the commanded velocity as the measured velocity even when the joint sits on a limit. What is wrong?
options: The velocity should be filtered, so that the controller never sees a sudden jump at a limit.
Nothing is wrong; the commanded velocity is the best available estimate of the measured velocity.
Velocity should always be zero in a mock, so that the controller never reacts to it.
State must report actual motion (displacement per period), or the controller thinks a stuck joint is moving.
questions.skillLabel: Consistent state from a mock interface

questions.prompt: A strict controller switch request fails because one activation conflicts. What is the state afterwards?
options: Only the deactivations were applied; the new activations failed.
Unchanged: all previously active controllers remain active.
Only the first activation was applied, before the conflict was found.
All controllers are stopped until the request is retried.
questions.explanation: Atomic switching leaves the system unchanged on failure.

questions.prompt: Where would you enforce velocity and position limits in a ros2_control setup and what would a mock test check? Mention state consistency.
rubric: Discusses limits in the hardware interface and in controllers with their pros and cons.
Lists mock invariants: clamped command, position in range, finite commands only.
Includes state consistency: velocity equals actual displacement over the period.
questions.skillLabel: Consistent state from a mock interface
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
